correctness.rationale: The direct exact Walsh test is wt(f+u·x) ∈ {6,10} for each u, since W=16−2wt. An independent enumeration obtains 896 functions, 448 of each support size, and confirms by binary Möbius inversion and polar-radical tests that each is a nonsingular affine quadratic. For every support, the exact trace set is {S ∩ supp(f)}; its cardinality reaches 2^|S| precisely on the proper ten-block subfaces. Independent checks validate all 512 witness entries, the entire f-vector, the seven-/eight-point exclusions, and the affine orbits of sizes 4480 for the nine-faces and 30, 840, 1920 for the unshattered eights. Both dimensions equal nine: the nine-face supplies a fixed-order tree, and any depth-ten complete tree needs 1024 distinct concepts, one per leaf.
residual_risks: Exact finite result on 16 points; no higher-dimensional extension.

value.rationale: Four variables are a natural small setting for full-rank quadratic bent functions. The classification replaces all Boolean trace tests by an affine-block containment criterion, distinguishes two different small obstruction mechanisms, and explains why all maximal supports have one orbit even though many seven- and eight-supports fail. That is independently useful for studying projections of this canonical nonlinear code, beyond publishing a known concept count or a dimension bound.
residual_risks: The value is the exact structural finite classification, not a general theory or a new eight-point spectral partition.
